children: India's central bank said on Wednesday it had attracted $136.38 billion inflows under its forex swap facility as of August 31, with most of these coming via a dollar deposit scheme aimed at the diaspora.
Banks in India received $127.23 billion via foreign currency non-resident deposits, $3.89 billion via external commercial borrowings and $5.26 billion through overseas foreign currency borrowings.

In June, the Reserve Bank of India introduced a set of measures, including concessional swap facilities aimed at attracting foreign currency to shore up the rupee, which fell to record lows earlier this year.
While the dollar deposit scheme was scheduled to close at the end of September, the central bank chose to end it earlier on August 31. The window for bank borrowings remains open.
